staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout. `sample_info.json` separately reports metadata vulnerable commit `7f0c3bb1bd8645ca556125b5afae8db77f973085`, but the staged tree's line map matches the saved ASan trace (`flb_parser_time_lookup` at `src/flb_parser.c:765` and `_conv_num` at `src/flb_strptime.c:674`) and is the exact vulnerable source traced here.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42488123 (fluent-bit): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target flb-it-fuzz-parser_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42488123
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / exact staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 100-byte witness is consumed by `tests/internal/fuzzers/parser_fuzzer.c` as a 42-byte configuration prefix and a 58-byte parser payload. In project code, `flb_parser_create()` consumes that prefix-derived configuration, sets `parser->type = FLB_PARSER_LOGFMT`, copies `time_fmt` as the six-byte string `25 73 2e 25 64 0b` (`%s.%d` followed by a literal vertical-tab byte), copies `time_key` as the two-byte string `eb f5`, and because `time_fmt` contains `%s`, sets `parser->time_with_year = FLB_TRUE`. On the second pack-enabled pass through `logfmt_parser()`, the payload's final bytes materialize the pair `eb f5=80446.`. Because that key matches `parser->time_key`, `logfmt_parser()` forwards the six-byte unquoted value slice `80446.` into `flb_parser_time_lookup()`. In the vulnerable `time_with_year == FLB_TRUE` path, `flb_parser_time_lookup()` skips the safe `tmp` copy used by the `time_with_year == FLB_FALSE` branch and passes that bounded slice directly to `flb_strptime()`. `flb_strptime()` parses `%s` from the digits `80446`, consumes the trailing literal `.` as the last in-bounds byte, and advances its cursor to one past the caller's six-byte slice. The next format directive is `%d`, so `_flb_strptime()` calls `_conv_num()` on that one-past-end pointer and `_conv_num()` immediately dereferences `**buf`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read of size 1 at `src/flb_strptime.c:674`. The staged patch closes this path by copying `time_ptr` into `tmp`, appending a NUL terminator, and updating `time_ptr/time_len` before calling `flb_strptime()`.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the fuzzed configuration prefix. `flb_parser_create()` sees `format == "logfmt"` and stores `FLB_PARSER_LOGFMT` in the parser object, which later makes `flb_parser_do()` route the payload into `logfmt_parser()`.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 100 bytes with SHA-256 `e48d5e48317601da98c81496a9c8b0172cd2fc398489c66e6e88e5515a4a3608`. Static replay of `parser_fuzzer.c` shows that bytes 0..41 are consumed as parser configuration before the project parser object is created: byte 0 (`0x7f`) selects `format = "logfmt"`; bytes 1..15 are copied into the temporary `time_fmt` buffer, whose first in-band NUL at file offset 7 makes the resulting C string `%s.%d` followed by literal byte `0x0b`; bytes 17..31 are copied into the temporary `time_key` buffer, whose first in-band NUL at file offset 19 makes the resulting C string `eb f5`; and the odd decoder-control bytes at offsets 36..41 take the second-decoder branch, leaving the remaining payload at file offsets 42..99. Step 1 is the first project statement that consumes that prefix-derived state.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the vulnerable time-string slice is materialized. After the matching `eb f5` key's `=` delimiter, the unquoted-value branch aliases file offsets 94..99 as `value = "80446."` and computes `value_len = 6`; because `c` reaches `end`, that slice has no in-buffer NUL terminator.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After parser creation set `parser->time_with_year = FLB_TRUE`, the else-path in `flb_parser_time_lookup()` leaves `time_ptr` aliased to the bounded six-byte slice `80446.` and forwards it directly to `flb_strptime()` even though logfmt values are not NUL-terminated C strings. The fix adds the missing temporary copy and explicit terminator immediately before this call.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `_conv_num()`'s first digit test dereferences the byte immediately beyond the caller's six-byte time slice while trying to parse the `%d` field that does not exist.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `READ of size 1` at `/src/fluent-bit/src/flb_strptime.c:674:6` on address `0x60b000000204`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 100-byte testcase allocation `[0x60b0000001a0, 0x60b000000204)`.

parser_admitted.description: The configuration state created in `flb_parser_create()` makes `flb_parser_do()` dispatch the trailing 58-byte payload into `flb_parser_logfmt_do()` instead of the regex, JSON, or LTSV handlers.

fine_trace.var: format, time_fmt, time_key, data, size, fuzz_parser
fine_trace.note: Static replay of the exact 100-byte witness shows that the harness consumes bytes 0..41 before this call. Byte 0 selects `format = "logfmt"`; bytes 1..15 and 17..31 are copied into the temporary `time_fmt` and `time_key` buffers; bytes 36..41 take the second-decoder branch; and `data,size` here then refer to the remaining 58-byte payload at file offsets 42..99. This harness boundary passes the prefix-derived strings into `flb_parser_create()` and later passes the trailing payload into `flb_parser_do()`, but it is not the scored source.

Source. `format` from step 0 is the literal string `logfmt`, so this branch stores `FLB_PARSER_LOGFMT` in the parser object. That state is later used by `flb_parser_do()` to dispatch the trailing payload down the logfmt-only path.

The attacker-derived `time_fmt` string is non-NULL and begins with bytes `25 73 2e 25 64 0b 00`, so this copy makes `p->time_fmt` and `p->time_fmt_full` the six-byte C string `%s.%d` followed by literal byte `0x0b`.

Because step 2's copied format contains `%s`, this branch marks the parser as an epoch parser and sets `p->time_with_year = FLB_TRUE`. Later `flb_parser_time_lookup()` therefore reaches the else-path that uses `parser->time_fmt` directly instead of prepending a year into `tmp`.

The attacker-derived `time_key` string is non-NULL and begins with bytes `eb f5 00`, so this copy makes `p->time_key` the two-byte C string `eb f5`. That stored key is later compared against each logfmt key slice.

On the second, packing pass through `logfmt_parser()`, after garbage byte `0x04` at file offset 90 is skipped, this scan treats file offsets 91..92 as identifier bytes and materializes the final key slice `eb f5` with `key_len = 2`.

After the matching key's `=` delimiter at file offset 93, the unquoted-value branch aliases file offsets 94..99 as `value = "80446."` and advances `c` to `end`, so `value_len = 6` and the slice ends exactly at EOF with no in-buffer NUL terminator.

fine_trace.var: parser->time_fmt, time_key, key, key_len, value, value_len, do_pack
fine_trace.note: During the second `do_pack == FLB_TRUE` pass, this predicate is true: step 2 supplied non-NULL `parser->time_fmt`, step 4 supplied `time_key = eb f5`, step 5 produced `key = eb f5` with `key_len = 2`, and step 6 produced `value_len = 6`. The parser therefore selects the time-lookup path for `80446.` instead of leaving the pair on the ordinary packing path.

This guard is false because step 3 set `parser->time_with_year = FLB_TRUE`, so the branch that prepends the current year and copies the timestamp into `tmp` is skipped. `time_ptr` still aliases step 6's six-byte slice `80446.` and `time_len` remains 6 when control reaches the else-path.

depends_on.via: parser->time_fmt && key_len == time_key_len && value_len > 0 && !strncmp((const char *)key, time_key, key_len)

fine_trace.note: Root cause. After step 8 leaves `time_ptr` aliased to the non-NUL-terminated six-byte slice `80446.`, this else-path call hands it directly to `flb_strptime()` using `parser->time_fmt` instead of first copying it into `tmp` and appending `\0`. The staged patch inserts that missing copy/termination before this call.

At entry, `bp` points to step 6's slice `80446.`. `_conv_num64()` consumes the digits `80446` and stops at the literal `.` that is still inside the six-byte buffer, so after this `%s` case `bp` points at the final in-bounds byte.

The next format character after `%s` is literal `.`. Comparing that literal against the current `*bp` succeeds on the final in-bounds byte `'.'`, and the post-increment advances `bp` to the first byte past the six-byte slice because no bytes remain after the dot.
The format still contains `%d` after the dot, so `_flb_strptime()` immediately passes step 11's one-past-end `bp` into `_conv_num()` to parse a day-of-month that is not present in the caller buffer.

Sink. `_conv_num()`'s first digit test dereferences `**buf` even though step 12 passed a one-past-end pointer. AddressSanitizer reports that read at `0x60b000000204`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 100-byte testcase allocation `[0x60b0000001a0, 0x60b000000204)`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the overread on the 100-byte heap buffer that libFuzzer allocates for this testcase before invoking the harness.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, and the staged vulnerable source

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the libFuzzer testcase buffer, and the traced root cause explains why project code reads one byte past that external 100-byte allocation after forwarding a bounded logfmt value slice into `flb_strptime()` without appending `\0` first.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-grounded to this path: it copies `time_ptr` into `tmp`, appends `\0`, and updates `time_ptr/time_len` before `flb_strptime()`. Stage 02 did not execute a fixed build for this sample, so `patch_resolves` remains false here.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42488123 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` with stack `_conv_num -> _flb_strptime -> flb_strptime -> flb_parser_time_lookup -> logfmt_parser`, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 42488123.

format.name: 100-byte parser_fuzzer witness with trailing `eb f5=80446.` time field
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 100-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `e48d5e48317601da98c81496a9c8b0172cd2fc398489c66e6e88e5515a4a3608`). The harness consumes bytes 0..41 as configuration, and in project code `flb_parser_create()` uses that prefix to set `parser->type = FLB_PARSER_LOGFMT`, copy `time_fmt` bytes `25 73 2e 25 64 0b`, copy two-byte `time_key` `eb f5`, and set `parser->time_with_year = FLB_TRUE` because the copied format contains `%s`. The remaining 58 bytes become the parser payload. On the second pack-enabled `logfmt_parser()` pass, the final payload bytes are file offsets 91..99: `eb f5 3d 38 30 34 34 36 2e`, i.e. key `eb f5`, `=`, and value `80446.` ending exactly at EOF. This makes `logfmt_parser()` call `flb_parser_time_lookup(value="80446.", value_len=6)`, and because the vulnerable code does not append a terminator before `flb_strptime()`, `_flb_strptime()` consumes `%s.` and then `_conv_num()` probes one byte past the 100-byte testcase allocation while trying to satisfy the next `%d`. Stage 01 only proves this exact blob and observed path; this contract does not generalize to nearby parser configurations, alternate time keys, or other logfmt value suffixes.
